مَوْقِتٌ , [of the measure] مَفْعِلٌ from الوَقْتُ: (S, K:) [it may therefore be an inf. n., or a noun of place, or a noun of time]. El-'Ajjáj says, “وَالجَامِعُ النَّاسَ لِيَوْمِ المَوْقِتِ
” [And He who congregateth mankind for the day of the appointment of a particular time, or, of the place of a certain event, or, of the time of a certain event; i. e., for the day of resurrection]. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
